body:
Read the full diff (23 files, +1266/-135) against the TOC. The identity probe is wired in the right place: it runs in invoke after the --print return and before both the repair loop and the one-shot launch, so --print spawns nothing and a refusal starts no agent. The launcher records the probe only on a passing check. The shipped table, the BuiltinAgentNames list, the 32-row count in the changeset, and the usage and docs name lists agree.

Nothing here blocks the merge. Four non-blocking points:

1. The timeout branch in probe() checks pctx.Err(), which is also non-nil when the parent context was canceled, so an interrupt during the probe reports "timed out" instead of canceled.
2. The match text for bob and kilo is "run", and for fx it is "ask". Those are common words, so a clashing tool whose help mentions them passes the identity check.
3. An operator row with probe_args set to [] is accepted, and probe() then skips the check silently.
4. The agent-mismatch hint says to define the agent in settings.json, but a shipped name cannot be redefined, so the operator has to choose a new name and pass --agent with that name. The hint does not say so.

I did not run the Go test suite. The test run was refused by the sandbox, so the test results are unverified.

comments.body: pctx.Err() is non-nil when the parent context was canceled as well as when the probe budget ran out, so a Ctrl-C during the probe is reported as "timed out" and refused as agent-mismatch rather than as canceled. Check ctx.Err() first, or compare against context.DeadlineExceeded on pctx, so the two cases stay separate.

The match text "run" is a common word and is checked as a substring of the combined help output, so any clashing tool whose help mentions "run" passes the identity check. The same applies to fx at line 210 with "ask". Consider a more specific match such as the exact subcommand usage line, or document that the probe only rules out tools that fail the help command.

A personal row with probe_args set to [] passes validation because agentProbeFields only requires probe_match, but this guard returns early on an empty ProbeArgs, so the row launches with no probe at all. Either reject an empty probe_args in config or document that an empty list disables the probe.

The hint says to define the agent in settings.json with an absolute binary path. A shipped name cannot be redefined (bad-settings), so the operator has to choose a new name and then run --agent with that name. The manual says the same thing. Say that the new name must differ from the shipped one.
